rule: Definitions and sign conventions fixed before any comparison is computed. A definition is not evidence: it says how a number would be formed, not that any number exists. Functions of the same names in basis.py implement them and take the reference conditions as explicit arguments.

frame_and_stations.axis: Rotor axis is +Z of the geometry frame; angular velocity omega = rotation_sign * 2 pi N / 60 in rad/s.
frame_and_stations.station_1: Compressor inlet measurement section, outside the rotating-frame zone.
frame_and_stations.station_2: Compressor outlet measurement section, outside the rotating-frame zone.
frame_and_stations.averaging: Total pressure and total temperature at a station are mass-flow-weighted averages over the section. With the constant-Cp gas model this makes the total-temperature rise consistent with the total-enthalpy flux of the existing audit. The choice is fixed here, before application; an area average is a different quantity.
frame_and_stations.pressures: Absolute pressures in Pa. Gauge values are converted before use and the ambient value is stated.

quantities.definition: Mass flow through the compressor, an output of the solver at imposed back-pressure, integrated over station 1 and station 2; the two must agree within the prescribed imbalance. It is never imposed.

literals: Mass flow rate in kg/s, an output of the solver at imposed back-pressure

quantities.definition: m_dot_corr = m_dot * sqrt(T01 / T_ref) / (p01 / p_ref). Always reported with its (T_ref, p_ref) pair.
N_corr = N / sqrt(T01 / T_ref), with the same T_ref as the corrected mass flow.
pi_tt = p02 / p01, both absolute total pressures at stations 2 and 1. It is not the outlet-static over inlet-total ratio that the historical case generator takes as an input.
Total temperature at station 1. In the historical case it is imposed by the totalTemperature inlet condition.
Mass-flow-weighted total temperature at station 2, an output of the solver. With adiabatic walls it carries the whole work input; that wall condition is itself an assumption.
tau = -M_z, where M_z is the fluid-on-rotor moment (pressure plus viscous) about +Z on the rotor patch. In steady state it is the torque the shaft applies to the wheel.

literals: M_z is the native fluid-on-rotor moment (pressure plus viscous) about +Z on the rotor patch

quantities.definition: P = omega * tau = -omega * M_z. It must be positive for a compressor and equal the net outward total-enthalpy flux within the prescribed energy imbalance; the sign is kept, never hidden by an absolute value. It excludes bearing, seal and disc-friction losses outside the domain.

eta_tt = (pi_tt^((gamma - 1) / gamma) - 1) / (T02 / T01 - 1), for the constant-gamma perfect gas of the model. It is an adiabatic-wall model efficiency of the idealised domain, not the efficiency of a physical turbocharger.

reference_conditions.why: The only flow reference already adopted by a repository register; reusing it avoids a third convention.

other_references_in_the_corpus.note: Reference stated on a published map of another unit.
The hypothetical inlet state of the historical case; an operating hypothesis, not a correction reference.

reference_conditions.conversion_rule: A corrected value is compared with another only after both are brought to the same (T_ref, p_ref).

model_constants.derivation: gamma * gas_constant / (gamma - 1), as the generator writes it

illustration_from_assumed_inputs.note: Shows what the conventions do to the hypothetical operating point. No flow, torque, power or efficiency exists to report.

independent_check.claim: corrected_mass_flow reproduces the 20 illustrative points of the 2026-10-02 research register from their stated inlet state and reference.

unregistered_leads.lead: SAE J1826, turbocharger gas-stand test code
unregistered_leads.note: Named from general knowledge as the usual home of gas-stand corrections; no value is taken from it.

unregistered_leads.note: Named from general knowledge; no definition is taken from it.
